chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"His guardian fasts on behalf of the child if he does not find a sacrificial animal."

key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: the child; a minor who is the subject of the ruling
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial animal offered in the rites of hajj
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his guardian; the person responsible for acting on the child's behalf
key_terms.يَصُومُ: fasts; performs sawm as a ritual obligation

ai.seo_question: What should be done for a child performing tamattuʿ hajj if no sacrificial animal is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a child in the context of hajj when a sacrificial animal is not available. It states that the child's guardian performs the required fasting on the child's behalf, indicating the guardian's responsibility in fulfilling certain ritual obligations connected to the child.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3102 - Abdul Rahman ibn Ayan narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "
A guardian should fast on behalf of a child if the child does not have a sacrificial animal."
